utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated. And may it be a very good morning. When we look at our Livenote system, normally reliable, we can identify the case to be called immediately. It is the 80th day of the Prosecutor's case. And I think somewhere it's correct to say enough is enough. Let's proceed in this way, but first hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning. Nicholas Koumjian with Ruth Karper for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In order to reach this goal, to finalise today, I have to inform you on the decisions by the three Judges yesterday on the Prosecution's seventh and eighth notice for admission of transcript pursuant to Rule 92 bis. The Chamber rejects Prosecutor's seventh notice for admission of transcript. We know in this case to a certain extent the OTP is not responsible for this late filing because one prerequisite was a decision by the President of this Tribunal. And therefore, it couldn't come earlier. But unanimously we held that it wouldn't give substantial added value, and balancing this against the right of the accused to have a cross-examination, we thought in the spirit of having a fair trial, it is not appropriate to have this under Rule 92 bis, especially when we are aware that it's not possible to have this witness here in The Hague for cross-examination. A little bit different is our decision on Prosecution's eighth notice for admission of transcript. This is the transcript of Mr. O'Donnell's testimony from the Simic case relating to the so-called variant A and B document, Exhibit SK39 in our case. Here, I would ask, and therefore I touch upon this point already now, that the parties may confer during the break. We have two options. Either, for the purposes of a fair trial, to give the Defence an additional possibility to have a cross-examination of Mr. O'Donnell, also as regards this special and, to a certain extent, important document. But this can't, as we heard yesterday, be done today. Maybe there is a movement or a change since yesterday. Otherwise, we have to go to the bitter end and to cross-examine or to grant the possibility of a cross-examination on Tuesday morning immediately before our deliberations. So these are both options, and may the parties please tell us which option they do prefer. And anything else to be discussed before starting with Mr. Sebire?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just that we did confer. I don't know if the Defence has a decision regarding the -- Mr. O'Donnell. But I gave them some additional information this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Mr. Koumjian and I did speak on the telephone this morning in connection with some of the issues raised by the Court, however we would like to reserve our comments for after Mr. Sebire's testimony so that we could present it to the Court fully and after consultation with our client during the Status Conference. But we do have specific objections, and are enormously disappointed in the tactics that are being utilised here. So instead of utilising the time this morning, I think it would be more appropriate to call Mr. Sebire, to have the OTP rest their case as scheduled, as ordered by the Court, and then to proceed with these other, what I would consider to be, procedural and maneuverable tactics which remain with the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't hope that you want to call the decision of the Trial Chamber as -- fortunately enough, we can't read it from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My comments were directed to the OTP, Your Honour. I suggested that directly as it relates to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to escort Mr. Sebire into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sebire. This is not a continuation but a new start of the testimony. Therefore, may I ask you once again to take the solemn declaration. Will you please stand up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, does the Office of the Prosecutor want to start with some questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Koumjian: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, during your examination on the earlier occasion, you were asked to provide certain information. First, the Defence attorney asked you to give him a list of individual versus mass graves. Did you prepare a chart showing the number of sites that contained either one body, two bodies, et cetera, for each of the exhumations that you obtained information about that took place in or concerned persons from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I prepared this chart, and we can find it in the document bearing the number 01848865. We can read in this document the number of sites and number of bodies presumed -- bodies, found for each site. 148 bodies were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this document with the ERN number 0188865 receive the next exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we, please, hear the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: S366, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, Exhibit Number S366. Is it translated into a language the accused understands, or is it possible for the Defence to discuss it with your client on the basis of this English?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It is not translated in the language that the accused can understand, Your Honour, however we have discussed it with him and he is in appreciation and understanding of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear what this chart depicts, please tell me if I'm interpreting it correctly. So for example, two sites were exhumed in which no bodies were found. 148 sites were exhumed where one body was found. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then 35 sites were exhumed where two bodies were found, so there was a total of 70 bodies from these 2 sites. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In fact, in the form I think the counsel misspoke as to the number of sites. He says in 2 sites, there were 70. But, in fact, the chart seems to be rather clear that's it's -- of 35 sites, 2 bodies on average were found that comes up to 70. Even though the witness answered it's correct, it's actually should be examined a little closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness come closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Sebire, just for the record to correct my error, 35 sites had 2 bodies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. In the middle column, we can see 35. It corresponds to the numbers of sites in which for each 2 bodies were found, which makes a total of 70 bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were further requested to provide a chart showing the -- showing for each of the individuals named in the annex to the indictment whether or not these persons have been exhumed and identified, have been listed in the Prijedor book of missing persons, or a Court declaration of death has been issued for that individual. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have here a document beginning with the ERN number 01847970 and ending in consecutive order with 01848137. May this document be marked -- given the next exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S367.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Sebire, just to clarify that document, the book of missing persons data that you used was from the version that's earlier been produced in court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you recently received an electronic database from the authors of the Prijedor book of missing persons updating their information?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I did receive that database approximately ten days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the way, does that database include witnesses' personal information including addresses and telephone numbers?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many kilobytes that database is? I'm not sure if I am using the right word for a computer, but perhaps you know the right word.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say that the two major charts in which the information was entered contained one of the two -- contains approximately 6.000 kilobytes and the second one 2.000 without counting the 15 other charts in which information was entered through Excel so that we were able to make a link between various charts in the database.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the database is not compatible with the OTP computers except for a laptop that you were able to borrow?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to print out a list from the updated book of missing persons containing the names?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the time being, what I was able to extract from that database is a list of disappeared people, but unfortunately it is still not possible to indicate for these people the exact date and the place when they disappeared. The printed document is 14.000 pages, and it accounts for 3.200 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it's for technical reasons, not for the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. content, that you are not able to continue with this work and include this additional information. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. Your Honour, in the various charts, the information regarding the date and the place of disappearance refers to the victim through a code, so I have to go through different charts in order to find the exact code that corresponds to that victim and then to transfer the information. For the time being, it means that I would have to go through 3.221 victims in order to find them, bearing in mind that the chart containing the information received by the next of kin and the people who knew about them, that they were also entered. So many people had testified about their disappearance, and that means that it would really take some time to do this work.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please correct the previous number, 3.222 people. Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a document consisting of 96 pages which I believe has been distributed to all parties entitled "List of Missing Persons from the database Nastradali." May that 90-page document -- excuse me, it has not been distributed. May that be marked next in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May the parties and the Judges first have a look on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It has previously been disclosed a few days ago when it was printed -- excuse me, no it was not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note. Please change the figure 3.222 and change it to 3.221. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There have been now twice changes on the figure or the number of victims you would have to go through. Could you please repeat this number finally that we have undoubtedly the correct number you stated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you are talking about the names that I was to check with regards to the indictment list, I counted 771 names. With regards to the list of disappeared people such as we can see on the database of missing persons of Prijedor, I come to 3.221 entries. So I have 3.221 names, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Now the transcript is no longer ambiguous. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then I have some -- what is -- could you please explain what is the printout, what is database Nastradali? Why this name? Can you give us some more information on the basis of this? It ends with number 3.237 persons. If you could explain the history, the development of this document presented now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the two documents of 296 pages that were shown to you, that was shown to you, this document comprises a certain number of columns. The column to the far left is the identification number given to the victim according to the database. The following number is the ID number, identification number. The following column contains the last name followed by the first name, followed by the father's first name and the mother's first name, and also the mother's last maiden name, if it's known. The date the when the person has disappeared, the date at which the person was born, and where the person was born. Regarding the number of victims, the last figure that appears is 3.237 persons. As I said, that's in the far left column, and that corresponds to the ID number given to the victim. It does not represent the total amount of victims. If you look at the first page, you will see that we don't have number 16 on the first page. So all together, we have 3.221 victims, and some of the entries are not counted -- accounted for, either because the information was not entered correctly or because the records or the record of that person was erased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Until now, we don't have an idea where this database comes from [inaudible] why this name. I think it's necessary to give some, comments on this, towards the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The database was obtained from an association which published the book of disappeared people of Prijedor, and all the information contained in that book was seized from a database which was created for that effect. During the seizure, some verifications were made regarding the list of people that were declared missing, which is why there could be some changes between the present list and the list in -- contained in the book which was published in April 2002. With regards to the title Nastradali or victims, unfortunately I could not give you any explanation about that name. I do not know what is the meaning of that word myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You mentioned an association. Could you please tell us precisely what association this is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. It is the association alliance which across Bosnia brings together several organisations dealing with missing persons in different municipalities that are missing. So the association for the missing persons in Prijedor is part of this larger organisation which is call alliance. The association itself brings together people whose relations disappeared in the municipality of Prijedor. This association has its seat in the municipality of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I take it that this has nothing to do with the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, no. But I'd rather not give you a definite answer either yes or no. I on the other hand know that they cooperated with the International Commission for the Tracing of Missing Persons in Sarajevo which is responsible for organising the identification on the basis of the DNA for the persons. Of course, they managed to identify. And the association for missing persons in Prijedor also, I think, cooperates with the Commission for Missing Persons which is responsible for tracing members of families on the basis of blood samples to establish whether the persons exhumed come or do not come from the area of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Unfortunately, opposed to ordinary courts, I have to put the question to you: This association, is it composed of all ethnic groups of Former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know. As far as I know, because I do not really have the list of people who belong to this association. I can only talk about people whom I met and who are members of this association. From what I know, these are principally persons of the Islamic faith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And coming now to the persons included in this list, is it restricted to Bosnian Muslim victims only, or are there also included Serbs or Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I can answer in the -- affirmatively, that the list includes Croats from Bosnia. As for the Serbs, one would have to check it. It seems to me that there are also one or two persons -- one or two Bosnian Serbs on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you compare this list of missing persons with the last update of the Red Cross list of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I received that list only recently. I saw it only recently. And therefore, I had no time to either compare it or go through that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Finally, is it your own printout without any changes, or did you generate to a certain extent this document? For example, you mentioned that on page 1 in the list of missing persons from the database Nastradali, there is a gap between 15 and 17. Did you leave this out, or was it already done by this association?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The list that you have is such as it is in the database. I have not made any alterations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So how come that you can comment on the question why we don't have, for example, 16 and other numbers apparently missing in this list? What's the reason for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you look at the information in database, the database will give you an identification number. But this such number appears only once in a database. If during the verification you found out that this person has not been missing or, rather, that it has been found or that it corresponds to another person who has already been recorded, then one erases the information concerning that individual. But you cannot also erase the number, as it would create big confusion. So it has to do with the database itself, which assigns a number, a recording number, and when you modify, then you also modify the number of the persons who are registered there. And that is the difference between the database that I used, the information for persons declared dead. In some cases, the recording was made twice. And in this case, one eliminates the record, but the number remains. But it cannot be allotted to another person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it your conclusion or do you have a reliable source for this that, for example, it is done for the purpose that Mr. Jordan appearing as number 15 always have in this special list number 15, and the number is not changed when leaving out an earlier number. Is it correct? And where do you have this information from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And where can you read this or where can we read this explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the document with the list which you have in front of you, there is no such explanation. Now, I believe that an expert on databases will be able to explain that the identification number in the database of an individual is the number which was assigned to that person, and that number does not change. This number, for instance, allows, when you go into the database to consult information which concerns that person. I was just saying that there is a second table with information which was provided by family members or witnesses insofar as the missing person is concerned. And in this table, for instance, the victim or the missing person is indicated only by the identification number, which you can find in the table that you have before you. So that is the unique number attached to a person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It would be the correct conclusion that we have here 3.237, and from this, you deducted 16 missing numbers, and then coming to the total number of 3.221. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm tempted to answer yes. But I would nevertheless like to make it more precise. I did not alter the database. And when I printed, this -- these numbers were already erased. But I have not made any alterations, so that if you want to know what is number 16, I do not have that information in the database.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No, my problem is: How did you come to the number 3.221 whereas it reads here 3.237?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the manner shown in the list, I transferred the information from one table. And in this document, I could read the number of entries that were made and which corresponds to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. number of -- to the identification number of the victims. In this Excel number, I could check the actual number of the entries, and it totals 3.221.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please understand that I still have some problems with understanding the different lists. Would it be a correct assumption that it would be necessary to compare this list of missing persons from the database Nastradali with the list of missing persons compiled by the International Red Cross updated in the database evidently not yet totally accessible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This could be done, but one has to see first whether the systems are compatible, that is, whether the system used by the Red Cross is compatible with the database in the Nastradali list. It's a matter of time, of course. And unfortunately, I therefore cannot tell you how long would it take to make such a comparison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any further questions first from the OTP? Then the Defence can cover both the remaining questions from the last taking evidence as regards this witness, then from the line of questions by the Judges, and then there may be additional questions by Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just a couple.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, the list in S368 that is entitled "The 96 pages, List of Missing Persons from the Database Nastradali," this was taken from the electronic database you recently received from the organisation of the missing persons for Prijedor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have access or have you ever -- do you have access to an updated database from the International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer was not audible.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not have access to that database.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And may we finally hear the date when this List of Missing Persons from the Database Nastradali was composed or published? First composed, and then published.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the list that you have before you, the date when we received a copy from the database is September this year. I believe it was sometime around the 10th, but I would have to check. When we have a database, one has to say that it is something that is subject to evolution, that is, it could be updated daily. Therefore, the list of information that we have at present is subject to changes. Perhaps it has already been changed since the time that we received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But please let me know, when you open an ordinary file in your computer, you can read immediately "updated as at." What does it read there, the last update?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid I cannot answer that question for a simple reason: The database is in Serbo-Croatian. I do not read it. I do not know. Thanks to the help of people, I could get the translation of the information that you have before you. But unfortunately, the file and everything else, I do not understand at all. The translation does present a problem because one has to go between different tables. And as far as the date regards, as far as I know, when we open that database, then you cannot see a particular area where the date of its updating would be indicated. So I cannot give you a definite answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be honest, I can't understand your answer. Whenever you open a file, it is possible to identify the technical data of this file, how many kilobytes and so on. And there it reads "date of last change." And this would be the date necessary, and no doubt it can be identified immediately. And I'm not prepared to admit this weak document into evidence. But please, any additional questions by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Ostojic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, along with Branko Lukic, my name is John Ostojic, we represent Dr. Milomir Stakic here. Sir, you note in what has been marked as S366 a comment that states that the authors and scientists mainly do not agree about the number of bodies that a mass gravesite may contain, to be called as such. It's actually on the first full paragraph of this second addition to the report, S366. You provided to us, sir, the actual articles which reference the authors and scientists who disagree as to how gravesites should be numbered?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, and it is indicated it is very difficult to establish finally what is in a mass grave, how to establish it on individual. The scientists disagree as to how one can establish this number. Whatever the case, I have indicated the results with graves containing up to ten bodies or ten and more bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was a little different. Did you provide us with the actual literature which suggests that scientists and people who work in the area of exhumations actually disagree on how one would calculate gravesites?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is true. That is not included in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In reviewing some of your materials yesterday, both the list of annexes which you provide approximately 16 as well as this addition -- my question to you, sir, is if you can tell me how long it took you to prepare these lists, tables, and annexes as you refer to them?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to give you any time that I spent on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think, sir, that it would be reasonable that it would have taken you approximately a hundred hours to compile the data that you did in connection with the testimony that you provided here today as well as the testimony that you provided previously in connection with this matter? Do you think that's a reasonable estimate?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot say yes or no. I spent a certain time preparing this, a new list. But how long did I spent on this list or the previous one, I know that I spent a lot of time doing this but I couldn't put a figure, a quantity, to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me an approximation because the Defence is being, in my opinion, limited as to the resources for utilising experts for preparation of our case, and I'd like to just get an idea as to you, as an individual, how many hours you have spent with respect to this particular annex? Do you think you spent more than 50 hours on it?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I can only repeat what I replied before, to -- I'm afraid I would be making an erroneous evaluation if I gave you any -- a specific amount of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why I said just give me an approximation, if you can.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on one working day, one spends a certain time over this file and sometimes over other files that I'm responsible for. It is very difficult for me to tell you exactly how much time I spent doing one thing and how many minutes I spent doing another thing. As for the -- no, it would even be difficult for me to give you even an approximate figure. I simply am not able to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand why you can't. But help me with this, Mr. Sebire: Who in your department or at the OTP can help me find the answer to how much time you, sir, spent in preparing these annexes? If you can't tell us, name the individual for me who can.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said -- what I said was that I couldn't give you an immediate evaluation of the time I spent doing this, and obviously the only person who can answer this is myself. But I cannot give -- it is very difficult for me to give you even an approximate number now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back briefly to these articles where the scientists are disputing how one should number the various gravesites, you within this Exhibit S366 identified two specific sections. Is it fair -- or you tell me, sir: Is this your summary analysis of how the scientists and authors have decided to define these mass gravesites, either those containing sites of five bodies or less on one hand, and scientists who believe that a mass grave should be considered as sites containing less than ten bodies? Is that basically your summary of the literature as it relates to exhumations and identification of gravesites?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the first case, that is, with graves with more than six bodies, yes, that corresponds to the general definition provided by the science. The second one is mentioned here, and I do it to give an idea to produce a general picture. Without going further into the explanation, when a mass gravesite contains ten or more bodies, that can give you an idea about that place and the number of bodies that were exhumed. So the first number can be considered as purely information, or information sake. And as you can see, we have done nine exhumations and we found 144 bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me with this, sir: Did you make an annex or a table, since I know that's something that in the department seems to be fashionable of late. Did you, sir, make a table to identify the 148 sites wherein there was only 1 body found in each of those sites?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think you can find it annex 8 [as interpreted] to my first report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not in this report, correct? Not in this new report, it's annex 8 to your old report. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, annex 8 in your old report lists approximately, if I'm correct, was it 68 or 69 individuals? Let me get that. Give me one second. Annex 8, page 9, lists 69 individuals, does it not?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, insofar as annex 8 is concerned, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe I'm not asking an articulate question. I'll try to just break it down into a simple form so I can understand. It's by no means to suggest that it's a criticism. You found or your data provides that there was 148 number of sites. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Out of those 148 sites, in each site, 1 body was found. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That totals, based on your third column of your report, S366, 1 times 148 equals 148. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just interrupt. There is a misunderstanding probably caused by translation. On page 20, line 14, it reads: "Annex 8." The witness said, I think, annex 1. So may it please be corrected.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we get it clear, Mr. Sebire, the 148 names are listed in which annex?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no annex that lists 148 names. You will find in annex 1 the sites of exhumation, the number of exhumed bodies. That's what you will find there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I recognise that. And that's why I want to ask the question five Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. minutes ago. What annex do I need to look at to find the 148 names that were found in these individual gravesites that were exhumed? I asked you, I think, if you did that, you pointed me to an annex, which I misunderstood. You've clarified it. I appreciate it. But we look at the annex now based on the clarification, and it doesn't quite get me where I want to go. Did you, sir, prepare an annex listing the 148 individuals who were buried in these individual graves? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is no specific list listing those 148 names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lists that were handed out were lists that were compiled per incident. And those incidents were given to me by the Prosecution. And after my first testimony, I was asked to go back to those lists and to review them and to look only at the names of people who were reported missing or who were killed during those incidents. And this is why I presented to the Court those documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Help me with this: In your definitional phase or process in completing these reports, particularly Exhibit S366, how do you define a gravesite?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not too certain if I understood the French translation of what you just said. Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you define a gravesite?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depends of the number of bodies. If it's more than one body, obviously it will be a gravesite. Depending on the way the person was buried -- I'm not too sure that I understood your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to really make it a basic question. And I'm not asking you to define for me a mass gravesite or an individual gravesite. I'm looking for you to define the word "gravesite" if you know, sir. Your analysis seems to contemplate it, you have it in there. You seem to suggest, although I don't want to be presumptuous, but you seem to suggest it would depend on the number of bodies in the actual ground, does it not?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not really. If the number of bodies should be taken into account, the circumstances of the burying of the body or bodies and depending on the way the people were killed or the person was killed, of course, all these elements would have to be taken into account when one defines exhumation site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I couldn't agree with you more. But if we have a hole in the ground -- and forgive me for being so basic about this. If we have a hole in the ground, do you define it as a gravesite? Or does it have to have a body in it?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which? It has to have a body in it?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would answer yes, of course. If you don't have a body that's buried, I don't see how you can possibly not call that a grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with you. Why, then, do you list as two gravesites with no bodies in it and trying to inflate the numbers as to the number of gravesites that were purportedly exhumed? If there's no body in it, as you say, sir, why do you list two gravesites? Under your definition, we should reduce that not only from 261 as you told us several weeks ago, but it should really be reduced to 258, shouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because if you remember while we were discussing the Kevljani gravesite, the archaeologists found bodies, and they were able, through various traces, to show that there was actually a body there at some point. The fact that there is no body during -- at exhumation does not mean that there was not a body before. Well, if you ask me a question: If you necessarily have to have a body in order to describe it a as a grave, I would say yes. But if the grave was robbed or the body was removed, it's a different thing. You could have an individual grave or a mass gravesite without one single human remain. But indications can show us and experts that at some point it used to be a grave. Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it does, but you're not an expert in that area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I am an investigator. I work for the Office of the Prosecutor. I am not an expert. My report only summarises the work of people that was done by the Bosnian commission for tracing missing persons, archaeologists, and other colleagues from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In connection with what you just previously said moments ago that you would look to determine where the body was placed, how it was buried, of the 148 individual graves that you list on Exhibit S366, can you show me or point to me to the annex which would identify the position, cause of death, date of death, or any of that type of information with respect to those 148 individual graves?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you will not -- there is no annex for that. If it's -- if you allow me, I would just like to say that for -- for those 148 sites, 1 body was found, and we have not been able to establish a link between the incidents that are mentioned in the indictment and that particular body. If I cannot make a link and establish clearly the time of death or if these people who were exhumed are in direct or have a direct link with the people that are enumerated in the indictment, it's a different thing. And this is why this list was not actually included. Whether we're talking about a gravesite with one body or two bodies, it could be done. And in that case, I would be able to give you a list of 1.252 names for causes of death, whether they are known or unknown.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would have been an interesting list, but that's not the point here. With respect to these 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I don't think it's fair not to indicate that we told the Defence at the beginning, and Mr. Sebire and we did, that there's over 50.000 pages of documentation which is available to the Defence to inspect. Mr. Sebire's report is obviously a summary. But the implication that it's his fault for not including that data, it is available to the Defence any time to inspect. His report is obviously limited and it is not 50.000-plus pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed, I think this should be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the Defence knew approximately how much time it would take maybe to digest the information, we might be able to assess whether or not we should or should not. But be that as it may, may I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in my attempt last night to reconcile the various OTP witnesses that have been presented here and in trying to reconcile Dr. Tabeau's listing of the number that are missing, when I look at her report, she lists, and as she has testified I think consistently, 1.731 individual victims from the Prijedor Municipality. From your report, both the prior one and this one, you seem to give a range of approximately 1.054 to 1.252. You both, at least from my review of it, relied upon the same primary and secondary sources. Can you explain to me, sir, the discrepancy, not in number, but in how you can come up with a drastically different number than Dr. Tabeau?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. This witness is an expert on Dr. Tabeau's report. And in fact, even the question misstates Dr. Tabeau's findings as far as that number of victims because it does not indicate -- she indicated she linked 1.731 victims to the 1991 census, which is something Mr. Sebire has no expertise in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, don't exchange arguments at this point in time. Indeed, it's correct that it was not the remit for the witness before us to compare one report with another.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You list, sir, in your annex that according to the information that you reviewed and you relied upon that there were 99 individuals who are said to have died in combat activities. Do you see that? It's on annex 2 of your report, S367.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that something that I could rely upon as being a thorough analysis that's complete, or should I rely on another OTP witness, let's just pick a name, say, Mr. Brown, who said that there were 80 such persons who died in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Again, same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to, and I tread on some thin water here, Mr. Sebire, to turn to an exhibit that has not been asked to be introduced into evidence, that is not yet evidence, and that is the list, but I have a couple questions on it anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the purposes of the transcript, let's call it provisionally S368.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This provisionally S368 which is the list of missing persons from the database Nastradali, can you tell me, sir, when this list was completed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Already asked and not answered. We expect the witness to prepare this during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the ten columns that you prepared rather exhaustively of this list, can you identify for me or explain to me why you do not have a column of information such as date of when this missing person was last seen?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's what I tried to explain at the very beginning of the day today, is that this information is contained in a second chart. And that unfortunately, I was not yet able to transfer that information in the chart that you have before you, because the victims that -- because the victims are identified by their code number. So I have to go through a huge amount of documents in order to be able to transfer that information in to that chart and to eliminate the information, the information with regards to the people who have given that information, that is, to eliminate their name, their telephone number, and their address.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other data are you providing in this chart that you still haven't completed, other than the date of when these missing people were last seen?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The level of relationship between the person that gave the information and the disappeared person, the missing person, the number of identification of the person that gave the information; it's all that kind of data. And as I said, that chart is now available, but it was not yet linked to this one because when we talk about a missing person, in the chart which contains the names of the next of kin that reported the person missing, we have to take into account that we have all these informations to deal with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any other data, as you sit here, that you're going to include in this chart or table or annex as you call it?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated earlier, I was not able yet, on the one hand because I do not read the language, I do not speak the language in question, I was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not able to go through all the charts that comprise this database.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any other -- my question was, though: Is there any other data as you sit here that you are going to include or have included in this additional or new annex or chart that you have not completed yet?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that would be, according to me, preferable to indicate is the date and the place of disappearance, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree. Date of disappearance and place of disappearance. Will you, sir, in this chart that we have provisionally marked as provisional S368 include those two columns for us, both the date of the missing person was last seen as well as the place the missing person was last seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I object because it's not evidence. I don't know if he is tasking Mr. Sebire, but we plan to rest our case today. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may respond, Your Honour. I'm not tasking him to do it. I thought he was going to maybe even supplement it, but that's fine. I'm not asking him to do it. I think we'll stand on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Totally correct. It may be for the Defence later to go in more details or even the Chamber to ask for additional information, if necessary. But I think once again, step by step, until now, we can't even with certainty identify what we have before us. And I think this is appalling.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then before the break, may I kindly ask you, Mr. Sebire, to try to find out. You told us that it was in B/C/S, and I know on the basis of a lot of work and it was difficult for you to prepare all these documents we wanted to be provided with. But nevertheless, do us one final favour and try to find out with the help of a technician and a person of, yes -- able to speak B/C/S or to read B/C/S the date of the last update of this file you have received. This should be no problem. And if you can confirm this immediately after the break, then we can conclude your hearing and then decide on the admission of this document provisionally marked S368. So now it's for me, once again, to ask the parties "sine ira nec studio" to try to come to an agreement on the Prosecutor's eighth notice for admission of transcript. There are three possibilities indeed. One could say: Why now we are dealing with the testimony in the Simic case as of February 2002? And I hope it was only negligence in the entire office of the Prosecutor that we were only now provided with this. But we have to come to a final decision. And as mentioned before, one option is the Prosecution withdraws or, insisting, we would have to continue on Tuesday morning. Or taking into account that Mr. O'Donnell was already in the Simic case cross-examined, and I wonder if there would be any added value of a cross-examination because it's not specifically related to the Municipality of Prijedor and the case against -- versus Dr. Stakic. That would be of some added value to have this cross-examination. But it's for you to discuss this, and please let us know immediately after the break. We start again at 11.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. May we, Mr. Sebire, hear whether or not you were able to find out the date of this document Nastradali. It seems to be a translation of the word "victim."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last time this database was modified was on the 2nd of September, this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any additional questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is not the case. Then, I thank you for all your efforts. And you're excused. And may the usher please escort the witness out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the meantime, we have to discuss the admission. We know now at least the date. And we are aware that the value is limited to that extent that another file including additional information is today not available. Under these circumstances, any objections, under these reservations we are aware of?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With respect to provisional S368, we do have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please give some reason additional to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Our objections are three-fold. One, the document, as we just learned from Mr. Sebire, was prepared well in advance of the deadline that was imposed by the Chamber with respect to documents to be produced and submitted for admission. It clearly falls outside the deadline imposed by the Court last week. Secondly, as the Court I believe has noted, the document is not only incomplete, but by virtue of its incompleteness does not provide the Defence an opportunity to cross-examine the witness on issues that might be of significance. Third, which is a compilation of both one and two, we believe with the late filing and the fact that the Defence would be denied an opportunity to cross-examine on specifically the issues relating to the purported date that the individual was last seen as well as the place where the individual was last seen, we believe that that would constitute prejudice to the Defence and would not guarantee that the Defence would have a fair trial in connection with this exhibit and these issues. For these reasons, Your Honour, we ask that provisional S368 be denied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we submit to the Bench the document was provided because we received several communications through the Court's legal officer that the Chambers wished the electronic, the latest version of this book. The book, I believe, that is in evidence is, I believe, a 1998 version, six years after the conflict, and does contain the information that Mr. Ostojic was asking about. And there may be some slight difference in names. I think, actually there's about seven fewer names in the new database, so either duplicates were removed or some individuals were discovered, but we submit it to the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Knowing that this document is not a complete document, as there is evidently additional file giving more insight and facilitates the understanding of this document, with all these reservations, and bearing in mind that it will be possible during this case to have this additional information, this document is admitted into evidence as S368. We are aware of the limited probative value of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I be heard, Your Honour. Based upon the Court's ruling, the Defence would like, as we have previously requested and inquired, that it, too, be provided with the electronic form version of the material so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can we please come back to this point. I have still on the agenda access to this file. I don't know whether it's possible to print out everything or whether it's better to have access to this. We should discuss this issue, please, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's now turn to the eighth notice on the admission of evidence under Rule 92 bis. May I ask the parties: Did you come to an agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, we did discuss with the OTP the position of the Defence. The Defence attorneys have met and have consulted with Dr. Stakic in connection with that. We have decided that we will not be asking cross-examination questions to Mr. O'Donnell today or Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So in result, you don't object to the admission of these transcripts under Rule 92 bis. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we actually do object, as stated earlier. And we would like to stand on our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The objections with respect to the Prosecutor's eighth provisional motion - I know I'm not identifying it by its accurate name - we believe Your Honour for a number of reasons should not be admitted. As the Court well knows, the burden of proof is on the OTP to establish each and every element within the fourth amended complaint. At the commencement of these proceedings on April 16th, they had a witness who interpreted and gave some testimony in connection with the document, namely, as we have called it, the variant A/B document. The document at that time over our objection was admitted. At no earlier point could the OTP have known specifically that the defendants were going to object to this, but they certainly knew during the first week of April. The OTP has made a conscious decision not to call witnesses in connection with this document, despite our objections. The OTP also consciously made the decision to call a witness by the name of Mr. Bernard O'Donnell in this case relating to matters specifically with Dr. Stakic, and yet chose not to inquire about the document identified as variant A and B. The OTP apparently, in hindsight has now reviewed the testimony, the evidence that has been presented, and feel at the eve of the closure of their case in chief that there's some necessity, despite the fact that the document has been admitted over the objection of the Defence, to provide the Court with what we think is some additional evidence outside the parametres of this courtroom in connection with that document. The Defence will incorporate, as we did during the presentation of Dr. Donia's report, the reasons why, among others, we objected to the variant A/B report -- document. We think and continue to maintain that a proper foundation for that document was not laid. We believe that the document is not authentic, as we have highlighted in early April of this year, for a number of reasons. We believe there has been no nexus or link to this document by any witnesses who came from or around the Prijedor Municipality. We believe that there was a conscious effort by the military analyst not to review this document, despite the fact that he tried to opine under oath that there was some linking or relationship between the civilian and military authorities. One can only speculate why that decision was made, but given the opportunity, perhaps we can address the Court specifically our view on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this is not the point in time to exchange arguments. I see a certain ambiguity in your arguments. On the one hand side, you object to the admission into evidence of this transcript; on the other hand, you state that based on a discussion with your own client, you don't feel it necessary, as it was suggested and proposed, to cross-examine this witness also on the basis of this testimony in the Simic case. I think under Rule 92 bis, aiming at an expeditious trial, you can't have the choice to say on the one hand side: "No, we object." And on the other, at the same time, say: "But cross-examination is not necessary." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We believe that the OTP under the rules provided by this Chamber has been given a specific deadline, that being that they must close their case this week. We have made our objections with respect to the document. We are confident that we want to stay on those objections, or stand on those objections. We do not believe that at this late stage, given an opportunity to cross-examine would relieve the fundamental rights of both the accused as well as the obligation to proceed in having a fair trial before this Tribunal. We believe, as the Court has asked us several days ago, that the OTP, in fact, has waived their right to present that testimony, that the OTP, in fact, has waived their right to present that evidence. And if we look at 92 bis, the questions of unavailability of witnesses, the factors that constitute why a witness should or should not be brought live versus a 92 bis statement, I dare say and conclude that they are not met. The witnesses that the Defence has consistently throughout this trial, with the direction of Dr. Stakic stipulated to, there was a clear foundation that those witnesses are crime-based; that those witnesses have some issues, some personal, some in other forms and nature; that did not want to testify before the Court. The Defence accepted those, both suggestions by the OTP and incorporated the comments by the witnesses. Mr. O'Donnell does not come within those parametres.
