utterances.text: I apologise again. We already have -1 as a colour copy. So instead of 1 and 2 today, we would have 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Excellent. Thank you for this. So that the transcript is not ambiguous, 55294, S84-2. 55287, S84-3. Objections against this bundle solution?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence under the numbers mentioned before. Then it follows committee international de la Croix Rouge -- some Red Cross documents. And may I ask for some comments on the probative value of these documents for the case before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe what we were trying to do is to respond to requests from the Court regarding reports of international organisations, and I thought the Court might have mentioned specifically the Red Cross. These are simply a collection of the 1992 press releases, all of them that we have, from the Red Cross. Obviously, many of them do not relate to this case. Overall, they would go arguably to the widespread and systematic, but looking through these, there are only a few that would actually relate to even that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be possible to withdraw?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the next, Kozarski Vjesnik of 14 August, 1992. We have the English version, and this is in the war edition of Kozarski Vjesnik of -- where can we find the date here? 14th of April, 1992. The article in the three first columns in the middle, in the upper part of this Kozarski Vjesnik page, only this will be admitted. If there are no mandatory objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're just unclear, is it the 14th of August or 14th of April, 1992? Because we did not receive the 14th of April or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the document, it reads 14th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S374A and B respectively. Then I have some problems with the following documents: As I understood the policy of the Office of the Prosecutor until now, the following documents, especially the Prijedor report prepared by Sophie Hanne Greve and others, were the observed at the point of departure for investigation. But I think we discussed it earlier having not only these documents before us, but all available documents published by the United Nations on these issues. And it's not -- this list of documents is not at all exhaustive. But it's -- you can't really call it hearsay -- it's a report that led the OTP to investigations and the result of these investigations were presented in court, be it by documentary evidence, be it by witnesses' testimony. So therefore, I think it is not necessary and it's not of assistance, and it may reopen the case if the Defence, for example, requests an examination or cross-examination of Hanne Sophie Greve. And therefore, may I ask in this case first the Defence, what is your position on these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do have an objection to those documents, Your Honour. And in addition to those that the Court has indicated that we may, we also believe that the documents that the OTP specifically with Madam Sophie Hanne Greve, it falls well outside the parametres of the fourth amended indictment. It, in fact, discusses specifically our client Dr. Stakic in connection with dates in 1993 through 1996. We would strongly object to the admission of that document and those documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be possible for the OTP to withdraw having in mind that we have now far better evidence and more direct evidence than reflected in this United Nation reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, at least as far as the pre -- if I can deal with them separately. First, it was our understanding that the Chamber had requested these -- perhaps we misunderstood. The Greve report, I certainly would agree with you, it was not our original intention to present that, and although it certainly deals with factors of relevance here, we think we have presented much more direct evidence regarding the same events. So we have no objection to withdrawing that. As for the United Nations reports, we believe that these are relevant, particularly to the issue of deportations, because they do show a pattern particularly in northwestern Bosnia that the United Nations was trying to deal with throughout 19 -- the summer and fall of 1992 of mass numbers of individuals being expelled or deported from this area. And we think that the perspective of the agency that was trying to deal with this mass exodus is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You're referring now to the Mazowiecki reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, Mr. Mazowiecki's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Mazowiecki 1, 2, 3. I think indeed this is -- it is difficult to understand this as evidence because I think it's public domain, it's public knowledge, that these documents exist. And yes, may I have separate observations as regards these Mazowiecki reports, the three.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With respect to the report that the OTP has suggested has some relationship to the count relating to deportation, we do object. We think the evidence that was called is the evidence that they should rely upon and should not be supplemented by extraneous reports such as these. We also believe as we have suggested earlier that if they wanted to submit the report, it could have been submitted by one of their experts who dealt with specifically population movement and demography, Madam Dr. Tabeau. They chose not to. We believe they also could have submitted this document as possibly 92 bis. They did not. To submit the document now we believe, Your Honour, respectfully, would violate our rights to confrontation with the witness and our right to cross-examine the witness. We believe as a consequence of that that we would be denied our right to have a fair trial, specifically relating to that count, and specifically relating to those documents. So for those reasons, Your Honour, we would ask that the Court not admit the documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- can I just intervene at this stage, although Mr. Koumjian has obviously been dealing with it. Your Honour, I've had a look at them and I take the point that Mr. Ostojic makes, although they may be useful, we haven't been able to call a witness, they haven't been able to cross-examine on the source of this information. So we'll withdraw those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: These three are withdrawn. And hopefully the transcript reflects that I wanted to express at that point in time, I think it was in June when we discussed this issue, we deliberately asked the OTP whether or not it was the intention to tender these reports because we envisaged already at that time the problems emanating from this report. So let's finally come to the Prijedor report as such, prepared by Hanne Sophie Greve. Do you want to withdraw this document as well? Because to be honest, we have seen far more direct evidence and far more concrete and updated evidence than this final report dated 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was addressing earlier, and I think I made the exact same points that Your Honour just made. Again, it was perhaps a misunderstanding on our part but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we have a document, Bosnia and Herzegovina, January 1997, the unindicted, reaping the rewards of ethnic cleansing." May I hear -- it's apparently from Human Rights Watch Helsinski. May I hear observations by the OTP and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The material contained within that report, it is our respectful submission, goes far beyond the time parametres in the indictment. It also renders certain conclusions and opinions with respect to individuals that the Defence and Dr. Stakic would not have an opportunity to either test the voracity or credibility and would not have a right to cross-examine. We think we have heard exhaustively - although I'm cautionary in using that word - evidence in connection with Dr. Stakic, as well as the time period involved in the indictment. This report is a summary and conclusion of a group of individuals, or an individual, which we believe is not of assistance to the Court to reach a decision in a criminal proceeding such as this. It is for those reasons we would ask that the report not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Our strong recommendation here would also be that we do what is our mandate, and not to leave it to nongovernmental organisations. Can you agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the following pages, we recently discussed. These are the faxes we received. Then let's come to the -- that what one could call, once again, public domain. But for the purposes of this case, the Chamber itself alerted the parties that they could not rely on earlier decisions, especially as regards the Room 3 massacre. The only question is: Is it necessary to tender these documents available even on the Internet into evidence, or was it just for the purpose of that we know these documents -- if I could please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If I could just clarify which documents we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are discussing in the order first the document from the Prosecutor versus Kolundzija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, it's not our intention to offer those into evidence; they are clearly not evidence. The Defence raised several times a point in court that we think misstated the position of the Prosecution and we simply provided that to the Court, to the Chambers so that the actual agreements would be available. But we agree an agreement between the Prosecutor and a third party is not evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections as regards the authenticity of these nonsigned documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope, and please, let me know, Madam Registrar and also Ms. Karper, is there anything we left out today? Yes. S217, the CSCE report, Mr. Ostojic wanted to present his objections. This document is not admitted yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We objected to the submission of this report because we believe that the evidence that was led by the OTP specifically by the witness Mr. Bernard Mayhew -- no, Mr. Mayhew should satisfy any and all issues relating to the factual background of the involvement of the CSCE, their inspection. We believe this report goes a bit further than the testimony of Mr. Mayhew and covers issues not specifically led by the OTP. By way of example, we would direct the Court's attention to page 8 of that document where there is some discussion, if I can generally categorise it, as identification of persons or armies in uniform dealing with what they would identify as being recognised authorities. Without giving us a proper basis as to who those individuals are, both from the alleged army position and authorities. The Prosecutors did not lead that evidence. To admit this report, we think, would be prejudicial because it does involve facts such as this one which in our opinion do not and should not be given without the right to cross-examine the witness who made these conclusions or gave these opinions. And for those reasons, we ask that Exhibit S217A not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I find this a slightly strange objection, I have to say, because when Mr. Mayhew testified, he went through great parts of this report. Your Honours, it's clearly relevant; it clearly deals with the relevant period. Mr. Mayhew gave some evidence, as I recall, though I haven't refreshed my memory from his transcript, about that particular passage that's referred to and about what was seen, confirmed that he had read -- although he didn't write the report, and it accorded with his experiences, and he was probably the most experienced of anyone on this team. And as I say, given that great parts of it were read out in the transcript, I utterly without objection, Your Honour, I fail to see how the document itself should not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As to the fact that report served as a basis for Mr. Mayhew's testimony, and his testimony can only be understood in the context with this document, this document as such is admitted into evidence. We are aware of the objections by the Defence, and no doubt, the Chamber will restrict the use of this document to those parts referred by Mr. Mayhew. Admitted into evidence as S217A, B respectively. As regards S210, the Prosecutor promised to provide an updated index of photographs from 210-1 to 210-21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It can be distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That it is quite clear what we have before us, it should be marked S210-0. Document S337. There was a request that at least one copy of this report dated the 9th of September should be prepared in the new version including the corrections specified in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We have copies for everyone of the corrected version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And as we handled it earlier, S337-1. There are some outstanding translations, S303-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I look efficient, but I can't take credit. It's available, thanks to Ms. Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S254, translation of the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It has also been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: D12, in part, should be translations prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We do have the translated version from B/C/S to English of D12, which I think is a report, the military report, that was relied upon also by Mr. Brown, of Mr. Jusuf Ramic. We are still in the process of photocopying the accurate number of copies to be distributed. We hope to accomplish that within the next 45 minutes or shorter. But I must admit that we didn't have it personally translated. I think it was done through the translating department with the assistance of Ms. Ruth Karper, I believe, and we were given the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Actually, it was an OTP translation, to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I see this is a coordinated cooperation. S151-1, it was a transcript of video S157, the final translation. The same is true for S151 and 365.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We have it in the building. We'll try to locate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's time enough to distribute it during the day. And finally, S362, the 8317 Prijedor TO document. There was reference made, but until now it was only a draft translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's not ready yet, the final translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but only for clarification, it's still open. So then, may I ask first of all again, Madam Registrar, do you have any wishes to the party or the Bench? I think S61, it has been shown. It's fine. Ms. Karper? No objections. So please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Two points, Your Honour. I think there was one additional document that was submitted in that bundle, a single page, with the ERN number 01844975 that we have not yet dealt with. It's from the Internet. It's a report from the BBC, but with -- the source is the Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA. Again, the ERN number is 01844975.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have the English version but not the B/C/S. You have it in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It is not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But it will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S375A and B correspondingly. Any other jewels from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We do have translations of Kozarski Vjesnik articles cited in Mr. Donia's report or testimony for distribution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: These documents were already admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe the two parties agreed on which would be translated, and these are the agreed translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We haven't had an opportunity to verify that, but if we do we'll bring it to the Court's attention with respect to whether what's translated is that which we have agreed to. And if the Court doesn't hear from us, I guess we could presume that we would have no objection to those items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Finally, Your Honour, I believe this witness testify in open session. Dr. Cehajic had -- Your Honour had asked for the witness to fax us something, or the witness had faxed us a document which has now been translated. So it's available to be distributed, the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It has already an exhibit number. Correct? May I hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's our understanding that that is J2 -- no. Correction, correction. Perhaps it has not yet been admitted. We can check with Ms. Sutherland. I'm not sure if this was -- this may have been something she faxed after her testimony. Ms. Sutherland has sent an email indicating it was not yet an exhibit. I think the witness perhaps -- my memory is -- I'm not sure of it -- had mentioned that she would fax this at the request of the Court, and she did so. And now we have the document and the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it would be J18, or do we have it already? Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not with the document's admission into evidence, but we do have, if we can, at this point at least make a preliminary comment with respect to the translated version. We do believe that some of the words such as in the first paragraph where it mentions the lower court, that that is not an accurate interpretation because we hope in the Defence case, if necessary, to present perhaps some document similar to that. So we would like to have it at least consistent with what we believe is the accurate interpretation. With that reservation, we have no other objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, J18A and B respectively. From your side, any further contributions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. From the Defence, the side of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not on these matters, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then as this concludes now the Prosecutor's case, I have to ask Dr. Stakic, do you want to make any comments at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. As already discussed earlier, on request of the parties, there will be a 65 (i) meeting. And I think it's appropriate to have some refreshment at least. Is it agreeable for the parties that we start this meeting at 2.00 in Room M 149?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This concludes the Prosecutor's case at the 80th day of the case. And the trial stays adjourned until further notice.
